transcript:
Header: 2026-12-31 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Elena Park, Marco Diaz, Ravi Kumar (Redwood); Priya Shah, Liam O'Connor, Marta Ruiz, Daniel Ng (Clearpath)

Summary: quick security posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO controls, how we surface evidence, and specifics around RBAC/SSO, audit logs and KMS. Customer is evaluating dedicated vs private for PHI.

00:00 Elena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Elena from Redwood, AE on the account, with Marco and Ravi, our SE duo.
00:06 Priya: Hi, Priya here, Head of Security at Clearpath. Thanks, Elena. We've got Liam and Marta on too.
00:12 Marco: Quick agenda - cover SOC 2 and ISO documents, trust center access, controls mapping, then deep dive on SSO and KMS. Leave time for q&a.
00:20 Liam: Sounds good. Our main ask is to understand what evidence we get, how often, and whether Redwood can support our data residency + encryption requirements.
00:28 Elena: Great. At a high level we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering the inference platform and control environment; we also maintain an ISO 27001 cert. We surface artifacts through the Trust Center - think of it as a gated portal where customers can download the report, bridge letters, and mapping spreadsheets.
00:42 Priya: For the SOC 2, is the scope including dedicated and private deployments or just hosted? We need to know what applies to our contract.
00:50 Marco: Good question. Historically our SOC 2 scope covers Redwood's hosted production environment - the control processes for the shared control plane. For Dedicated we have a subset of controls that still apply, and for Private (VPC/on-prem) we provide a controls mapping that delineates responsibilities - some controls become customer managed. The ISO cert is similar: core platform controls are included.
01:10 Marta: When you say "controls mapping" can you show an example? Do you map SOC 2 criteria to specific config or artifacts?
01:18 Ravi: Yes, we produce a controls mapping spreadsheet that lists each SOC 2 CC criteria and ISO clause, the Redwood control owner, evidence location, and any customer responsibilities. We'll share a sample - apologies if the transcript later shows that as 'control's nap' -
01:32 Daniel: (laughs) mhm
01:35 Priya: How do customers get the reports? We have procurement rules about where reports are stored and who can access.
01:40 Elena: Through the Trust Center: we create a tenant-level access for your security contacts. It supports SSO. We can add Marta and Priya as viewers; access is logged.
01:48 Priya: Is that SSO via SAML/SCIM? We manage accounts via our identity provider.
01:52 Marco: We integrate with SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC in the Console allows role-based permissions - admin, security_viewer, billing, etc. We can also scope Trust Center access separately.
02:08 Priya: Audit logs - how long are they retained and can we stream them to our SIEM? We need at least 1 year of immutable logs for audit.
02:16 Marco: Default retention for platform audit logs in hosted is 90 days, but for enterprise customers we support configurable retention up to 3 years via the Dedicated plan, and for Private you manage retention. We provide log export/streaming to your S3/Cloud Storage or to a syslog endpoint; we also support Kafka endpoints for real-time ingestion.
02:34 Liam: For HIPAA/PHI, are logs considered covered data? Any PII in logs is redacted?
02:40 Elena: We redact sensitive content in application-level logs; audit logs record actions, user IDs (pseudonymized if required), and resource IDs. For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed logging to avoid any accidental capture.
02:55 Marta: Encryption specifics - at rest and in transit, and KMS. Does Redwood use a customer-managed key option?
03:02 Ravi: By default we encrypt at rest with provider-managed keys (AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault), and TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. For enterprise we offer customer-managed KMS where you bring your own key (BYOK) and we integrate with your KMS via external key wrapping or a CMK grant model. For Private, you control keys entirely.
03:22 Priya: Do you support HSM-backed keys or only software keys? Some compliance requires HSM.
03:27 Marco: We can support HSM-backed keys via Cloud KMS HSM offerings in the cloud providers; for on-prem/private deployments we integrate with customer HSMs using PKCS#11 or AWS CloudHSM equivalence. We'll include those details in the controls mapping doc.
03:43 Liam: What about key rotation?
03:45 Ravi: We support regular rotation policies; for BYOK we follow your rotation schedule and provide rotation instructions and migration guidance. We log key usage in audit trails.
03:55 Priya: Trust Center - is access single-tenant for us? We don't want cross-customer visibility.
03:59 Elena: Trust Center access is per-customer tenant. No cross-customer mixing. Everything is gated behind SSO and per-user RBAC.
04:06 Daniel: Can the Trust Center provide automated evidence pull? Like an API to download the latest report for internal GRC tools?
04:12 Marco: Not currently public API, but we can enable SFTP or a secure bucket sync to push latest artifacts; many customers script a pull from a dedicated storage bucket we can provision. We'll note that as a potential automation.
04:22 Marta: For ISO 27001, do you provide statement of applicability (SoA) or just the cert?
04:26 Ravi: We provide the cert and a SoA/controls mapping for enterprise customers under NDA. The SoA lists control implementations and evidence links.
04:36 Priya: Regarding compliance evidence, are pen tests part of the package? Any recent third-party pentest reports?
04:41 Elena: Yes, we do annual third-party penetration testing; we share executive summaries in Trust Center, and full reports under NDA. Latest pen test was in 2026-08 with remediation tracked.
04:52 Liam: Can you talk about network segregation for Dedicated? We need to know how isolated compute is and whether tenants share underlying hardware.
04:58 Marco: Dedicated provides dedicated GPU pools per customer - logical isolation, and where required we can provide physical isolation on request. Networking is tenant-dedicated with VPC peering or private link options. For stricter on-prem we provide a private deployment package.
05:12 Priya: A few nitty-gritty questions - is there an external auditor for SOC 2 Type II, and can we meet them?
05:18 Elena: SOC 2 is performed by an independent CPA firm; we can provide contact and the audit firm name. Typically we do not coordinate direct customer calls with auditors, but we provide the report and can arrange RAS (responsibility and scope) notes.
05:30 Marta: On RBAC, do you support fine-grained role definitions and custom roles?
05:35 Marco: Console supports built-in roles and custom roles with granular permissions. We can also do attribute-based access through SAML assertions.
05:44 Daniel: If we move to Private on-prem, how is patching handled? We need a clear SLA and a maintenance window schedule.
05:50 Ravi: For Private deployments we offer two models: self-managed where you handle patches with our guidance, or Redwood-managed with a support agreement where we push patches in agreed windows. We'll share our maintenance playbook.
06:03 Priya: A few questions from compliance perspective: evidence retention, change management artifacts, and who owns encryption keys?
06:12 Elena: Evidence retention - Trust Center preserves reports historically; we also keep internal archives. For change management, we provide RFCs and release notes; major changes impacting controls are communicated through SOC 2 bridge letters. Key ownership depends on deployment mode: hosted (Redwood-managed CMKs), Dedicated (customer CMK optional), Private (customer-owned).
06:34 Liam: Do you have any model for data residency enforcement? E.g., pin customer data to a region and prevent cross-region replication?
06:40 Marco: Yes, we have region pinning for data and workloads. For hosted customers we can restrict deployment to specific regions and disallow cross-region replication of data. Dedicated ensures the compute lives in the chosen region. For Private, it's within your environment.
06:58 Priya: One concern - audit log immutability. We need logs that cannot be altered by operators. How do you enforce that?
07:05 Marco: We support append-only storage for audit logs with write-once options using object storage immutability (S3 Object Lock) or by streaming into your own SIEM where you control immutability. Also we publish checksums and periodic snapshots to an external bucket if needed.
07:21 Marta: Do you keep a change history of RBAC grants and admin actions?
07:24 Ravi: Yes, role grants and admin actions are logged in audit trails with timestamps and actor IDs; we retain change history per retention policy and can export it.
07:33 Daniel: For encryption in use for KV cache or model state, any specifics? There was a mention of KV cache earlier in docs and sometimes transcribed as 'kay vee cache'.
07:43 Marco: Yes, KV cache content is ephemeral and encrypted in transit and at rest. For Dedicated we can configure separate encryption keys per customer.
07:52 Liam: On legal and procurement - what contractual clauses do you typically include for data residency and breach notification?
07:57 Elena: We have SOC 2 attestations and standard incident response clauses: 72-hour notification, support for forensic logs, and contractual SLA/penalties on certain enterprise tiers. Data residency is specified in the SOW. Procurement usually requests additional addenda which we support.
08:14 Priya: Does Redwood support subprocessor lists? We need a vendor list for our vendor risk management.
08:19 Elena: Yes, we maintain a subprocessors list and will provide the current one in Trust Center.
08:24 Marta: A lot to digest. Can we get the timeline: we'll need all artifacts before our executive security review week the second week of January.
08:31 Elena: Absolutely - we'll try to get the SOC 2 and ISO documents and a controls mapping by Jan 5, and invite you to Trust Center.
08:37 Priya: For the follow-up technical bench, we'd like Marco and Ravi to run a short pilot with our infra team and sample PII data to validate no exfiltration and proper logging.
08:45 Marco: Sounds good; we'll scope that pilot and include network and logging telemetry.
08:50 Elena: Great. Any final quick questions?
08:53 Liam: One last - what about SLA for data deletion requests? We have CCPA/DSAR processes.
08:58 Ravi: We support deletion workflows; for hosted we can run deletion jobs and provide artifacts proving deletion. For Private, you manage deletion. Turnaround depends on dataset size; we'll include SLOs in the playbook.
09:12 Priya: Thanks everyone.
09:14 Elena: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.

Action Items Recap:
- Elena: Share SOC 2 Type II PDF, ISO cert, trust center invite, subprocessor list (due 2027-01-05)
- Marco: Prepare controls mapping and pilot plan for infra pilot (due 2027-01-07)
- Daniel: Send required regions and data residency constraints (due 2027-01-04)
- Marta: Confirm audit log retention and compliance owner contact (due 2027-01-06)
